title: Persimmons from next door
setting: Saturday morning outside a small apartment building. Yuki has come down to the mailboxes in her sweatpants, her washing still sitting in the machine upstairs. Next door, Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, is hanging out his laundry beside a basket of persimmons he has just picked from his tree.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu, yuki-san. kyou wa sentakumono ga yoku kawakisou desu ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます、ユキさん。今日は洗濯物がよく乾きそうですね。
lines.kana: おはようございます、ゆきさん。きょうはせんたくものがよくかわきそうですね。
lines.english: Good morning, Yuki. Looks like a good day for drying laundry.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. sou desu ne. demo kyou wa nanka, yaruki ga nai n desu yo ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます。そうですね。でも今日はなんか、やる気がないんですよね。
lines.kana: おはようございます。そうですね。でもきょうはなんか、やるきがないんですよね。
lines.english: Good morning. It does. But today I just can't be bothered.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dou shita n desu ka? shigoto ga isogashikatta n desu ka?
lines.ja: どうしたんですか？仕事が忙しかったんですか？
lines.kana: どうしたんですか？しごとがいそがしかったんですか？
lines.english: What's the matter? Has work been busy?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. konshuu wa zutto isogashikute, sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu.
lines.ja: はい。今週はずっと忙しくて、ストレスが溜まってるんです。
lines.kana: はい。こんしゅうはずっといそがしくて、すとれすがたまってるんです。
lines.english: Yes. It's been non-stop all week, and the stress has really piled up.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa taihen deshita ne. sutoresu ga tamaru to, yaruki mo naku narimasu yo ne.
lines.ja: それは大変でしたね。ストレスが溜まると、やる気もなくなりますよね。
lines.kana: それはたいへんでしたね。すとれすがたまると、やるきもなくなりますよね。
lines.english: That must have been hard. When stress piles up, your motivation goes too, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyou wa kaji o shiyou to omotteta n desu kedo, zenzen yaruki ga denakute.
lines.ja: 今日は家事をしようと思ってたんですけど、全然やる気が出なくて。
lines.kana: きょうはかじをしようとおもってたんですけど、ぜんぜんやるきがでなくて。
lines.english: I meant to do the housework today, but I just can't get myself going.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yaruki wa ne, hajimetara dete kuru mono desu yo. mazu wa chotto dake, yatte mitara dou desu ka?
lines.ja: やる気はね、始めたら出てくるものですよ。まずはちょっとだけ、やってみたらどうですか？
lines.kana: やるきはね、はじめたらでてくるものですよ。まずはちょっとだけ、やってみたらどうですか？
lines.english: Motivation, you know, comes once you've started. Why not try doing just a little first?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hajimetara, desu ka. demo, sono hajimeru yaruki ga nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: 始めたら、ですか。でも、その始めるやる気がないんですよ。
lines.kana: はじめたら、ですか。でも、そのはじめるやるきがないんですよ。
lines.english: Once I've started, huh? But I don't even have the motivation to start.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, uchi no kaki, douzo. tabete, genki dashite kudasai.
lines.ja: じゃあ、うちの柿、どうぞ。食べて、元気出してください。
lines.kana: じゃあ、うちのかき、どうぞ。たべて、げんきだしてください。
lines.english: Well then, have some persimmons from my tree. Eat them and cheer up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kaki! daisuki na n desu. uwaa, tenshon agarimasu!
lines.ja: え、柿！大好きなんです。うわあ、テンション上がります！
lines.kana: え、かき！だいすきなんです。うわあ、てんしょんあがります！
lines.english: Oh, persimmons! I love them. Wow, I'm getting all excited!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tenshon ga agaru, desu ka. omoshiroi iikata desu ne.
lines.ja: テンションが上がる、ですか。面白い言い方ですね。
lines.kana: てんしょんがあがる、ですか。おもしろいいいかたですね。
lines.english: "Tenshon ga agaru," is it? What a fun way to put it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. nanka mou, genki ga demashita.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。なんかもう、元気が出ました。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。なんかもう、げんきがでました。
lines.english: Thank you. I feel better already.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa yokatta. sutoresu ga tamatta toki wa, oishii mono ga ichiban desu yo.
lines.ja: それはよかった。ストレスが溜まった時は、おいしいものが一番ですよ。
lines.kana: それはよかった。すとれすがたまったときは、おいしいものがいちばんですよ。
lines.english: I'm glad. When stress builds up, something tasty is the best cure.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, yaruki mo chotto dete kimashita. mazu sentakumono, hoshite kimasu!
lines.ja: あ、やる気もちょっと出てきました。まず洗濯物、干してきます！
lines.kana: あ、やるきもちょっとでてきました。まずせんたくもの、ほしてきます！
lines.english: Oh, I'm even getting a bit motivated. I'll go and hang out my laundry first!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. yuki-san ga genki da to, watashi mo genki ga demasu yo.
lines.ja: いいですね。ユキさんが元気だと、私も元気が出ますよ。
lines.kana: いいですね。ゆきさんがげんきだと、わたしもげんきがでますよ。
lines.english: Good for you. When you're cheerful, it gives me a lift too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, jaa satou-san mo, tenshon agarimashita?
lines.ja: え、じゃあ佐藤さんも、テンション上がりました？
lines.kana: え、じゃあさとうさんも、てんしょんあがりました？
lines.english: Oh, so you're all hyped up too, Satou-san?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ee, tenshon agarimashita yo. hajimete tsukaimashita.
lines.ja: ええ、テンション上がりましたよ。初めて使いました。
lines.kana: ええ、てんしょんあがりましたよ。はじめてつかいました。
lines.english: Yes, very hyped. That's the first time I've ever said it.

choices.english: Satou-san offers to hang out Yuki's laundry for her, since she's worn out from work.
Yuki decides to skip the housework and rest today, as Satou-san suggests.
Yuki can't face the housework, but Satou-san's persimmons cheer her up and she goes off to hang out her laundry.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-8: after a stressful week, Yuki has no motivation (yaruki ga nai) and can't get going on the housework (yaruki ga denakute). In line 9 Satou-san gives her persimmons from his tree; she gets excited (line 10), feels better (line 12), and in line 14 goes off to hang out her laundry. A is wrong: Satou-san never offers to do her laundry; he tells her to try doing a little herself (line 7). B is wrong: he says motivation comes once you start, not that she should rest, and she doesn't take the day off: she starts with the laundry (line 14).

questions.english: It's Sunday and you just want to lie around. Kenta asks you, "nee, kyou nani suru? dokka ikanai?" Tell him you just don't feel like it today, using yaruki ga nai.
questions.ja: ねえ、今日何する？どっか行かない？
questions.kana: ねえ、きょうなにする？どっかいかない？
questions.romaji: nee, kyou nani suru? dokka ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you can't be bothered today: kyou wa nanka yaruki nai. With a friend ga can drop, and gomen softens it.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa nanka yaruki nai. uchi ni iru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日はなんかやる気ない。うちにいるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I just can't be bothered today. I'm staying in.

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa yaruki ga nai n da. mata kondo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はやる気がないんだ。また今度ね。
modelAnswers.english: I've got no motivation today. Another time, OK?

questions.explanation: In line 2 Yuki tells Satou-san kyou wa nanka, yaruki ga nai n desu yo ne (today I just can't be bothered), and in line 8 she says she doesn't even have the motivation to start (sono hajimeru yaruki ga nai n desu yo). About yourself, yaruki nai is a flat 'I don't feel like it'; about someone else (ano hito yaruki nai) it's a criticism. Avoid yaruki ga arimasen: it sounds stiff, and even politely people say yaruki ga nai n desu, as Yuki does. Kenta is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: Satou-san tells Yuki how motivation works. When does he say it comes?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、やる気はいつ出ると言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、やるきはいつでるといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, yaruki wa itsu deru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: After a proper rest, so she should take the morning off first.
Once she gets started, so she should try doing just a little first.
When she eats something tasty, like his persimmons.

questions.explanation: In line 7 Satou-san says yaruki wa ne, hajimetara dete kuru mono desu yo: motivation comes out (deru) once you start, so try a little first. Yuki uses the negative in line 6 (zenzen yaruki ga denakute, I just can't get going), and in line 14 it finally comes: yaruki mo chotto dete kimashita. A is wrong: he never tells her to rest; his advice is to start. C mixes up yaruki with genki: the persimmons are to lift her mood (genki dashite, line 9), and good food is his cure for stress (line 13), not where motivation comes from.

questions.english: You've had an awful day at work. Mai hands you a hot coffee and says, "hai, kore. muri shinaide ne." Thank her and tell her it's cheered you up, using genki ga deru.
questions.ja: はい、これ。無理しないでね。
questions.kana: はい、これ。むりしないでね。
questions.answer: Thank her and say it gave you a lift, in the past: arigatou, genki deta. It's about you, so it's deta; genki dashite is what you say to cheer someone else up.

modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。なんか元気出た。

modelAnswers.romaji: uwaa, ureshii. arigatou, sugoku genki deta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うわあ、うれしい。ありがとう、すごく元気出たよ。
modelAnswers.english: Aw, that's so nice. Thanks, it's really cheered me up.

questions.explanation: In line 9 Satou-san hands Yuki persimmons and says tabete, genki dashite kudasai (eat them and cheer up): genki dashite is what you say to someone else. In line 12 Yuki answers about herself: nanka mou, genki ga demashita (I feel better already), and in line 15 Satou-san says her cheerfulness gives him a lift too (watashi mo genki ga demasu yo). For 'that cheered me up', use the past genki deta. Don't answer genki dashite, which would tell Mai to cheer up, and genki ni natta usually means you've got over an illness. Mai is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Yuki sees the persimmons, what does she say?
questions.ja: 柿を見て、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: かきをみて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kaki o mite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?
questions.explanation: In line 10 Yuki sees the persimmons and says uwaa, tenshon agarimasu! (wow, I'm getting all excited!). Satou-san repeats it in line 11 as a fun, young-sounding expression and tries it himself in lines 16-17. B is the English speaker's trap: koufun shimasu sounds agitated or even sexual, not happily excited. C is the opposite, tenshon sagaru (get bummed out), which doesn't fit someone who loves persimmons. And tenshon is mood or hype, not 'tension' (that's kinchou).

questions.english: You've been working late every night. Your manager, Tanaka-san, asks you, "saikin, tsukaretemasen ka? daijoubu desu ka?" Tell him honestly that stress has been piling up, using sutoresu ga tamaru.
questions.ja: 最近、疲れてませんか？大丈夫ですか？
questions.kana: さいきん、つかれてませんか？だいじょうぶですか？
questions.romaji: saikin, tsukaretemasen ka? daijoubu desu ka?
questions.answer: Tell him stress has built up, politely since he's your manager: sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu. Stress piles up (tamaru); it isn't a verb you do.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, saikin chotto sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、最近ちょっとストレスが溜まってるんです。
modelAnswers.english: To be honest, the stress has been piling up a bit lately.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu desu. demo, chotto sutoresu ga tamatte kimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫です。でも、ちょっとストレスが溜まってきました。
modelAnswers.english: I'm OK. But the stress is starting to build up a bit.

questions.explanation: In line 4 Yuki tells Satou-san that after a busy week, sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu (the stress has piled up); he picks it up in line 5 (sutoresu ga tamaru to, when stress piles up) and again in line 13. Use tamatteru for how you are now. Don't say sutoresu shiteru: stress isn't something you do in Japanese, it's something that piles up. Hear the contrast in the scene: stress piles up (tamaru), while Yuki's mood goes up (tenshon agaru, line 10). Tanaka-san is your manager, so answer politely.
